question_text: A 36-year-old man is brought in by ambulance after being found down on the sidewalk. It is uncertain how long he was down before being found, and he did not have any forms of identification when he was found. On presentation, the man is found to still be unconscious with a disheveled and unkempt appearance. He is also found to be taking slow, shallow breaths that smell of alcohol. His temperature is 98.8°F (37.1°C), blood pressure is 106/67 mmHg, pulse is 119/min, respirations are 5/min, and oxygen saturation is 87% on room air. His pupils are found to be fixed and contracted, and he has multiple bruises and scars on his body. Which of the following sets of findings would most likely be seen in this patient?

                    ### Question
                    A 36-year-old man is brought in by ambulance after being found down on the sidewalk. It is uncertain how long he was down before being found, and he did not have any forms of identification when he was found. On presentation, the man is found to still be unconscious with a disheveled and unkempt appearance. He is also found to be taking slow, shallow breaths that smell of alcohol. His temperature is 98.8°F (37.1°C), blood pressure is 106/67 mmHg, pulse is 119/min, respirations are 5/min, and oxygen saturation is 87% on room air. His pupils are found to be fixed and contracted, and he has multiple bruises and scars on his body. Which of the following sets of findings would most likely be seen in this patient?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Decreased bicarbonate and decreased carbon dioxide
opb. Decreased bicarbonate and increased carbon dioxide
opc. Increased bicarbonate and decreased carbon dioxide
opd. Increased bicarbonate and increased carbon dioxide
ope. Normal bicarbonate and normal carbon dioxide

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Alcohol consumption can lead to respiratory depression, resulting in hypoventilation. This can cause increased bicarbonate levels and decreased carbon dioxide levels, leading to metabolic alkalosis. Therefore, the most likely findings in this patient would be increased bicarbonate and decreased carbon dioxide, supporting option opc.
